1.pericope_label: Hear my voice, O God, in my prayer: preserve my life from fear of the enemy

debates.q: What occasion does the psalm have?

sides.view: A complaint of the captives in Babylon, though the Syriac heading places it in the flight from Saul
None recoverable — it has no defined features, and the Daniel parallel fits only for that reason
The Passion of the Lord, and after it the sufferings of the martyrs
The question is left alone; the psalm is complaint and prayer ending in deliverance

debates.q: What are the secret counsel and the insurrection?

sides.view: Better rendered a secret league and a noisy gathering
Both the place of consultation and the counsel taken there
A plot first, then risings to carry it out, by men whose trade is sin
Matter for prayer: secret providence against secret counsel

outliers.view: Cite an earlier commentator who opened his exposition by announcing that the psalm title contains no history, abandoning the question before beginning
Observes that the devil is now bound, so that where the whole Church was once smitten together it is now tried through individuals

4.pericope_label: That they may shoot in secret at the perfect: suddenly do they shoot at him, and fear not

debates.q: Who is the perfect one shot at?

sides.view: David, and beyond him the Messiah and the church that is perfect in Christ
A man who apprehends no danger, ambushed so the aim cannot miss
The question is really about the shooters, who fear neither God nor man

debates.q: Is the text of the sixth verse sound?

sides.view: No — the versions and some manuscripts point to a corruption; read that they have completed their subtle measures
Yes, and its triple use of one verb is deliberate emphasis
The plain sense suffices: they study new ways of doing mischief

outliers.view: Derives the word investigate twice over, from stripping a man bare and from tracking a stag by its slot, and refers the reader to a hunting manual for the rules

7.pericope_label: But God shall shoot at them with an arrow; suddenly shall they be wounded

debates.q: What is the arrow God shoots?

sides.view: One of the four judgments — famine, pestilence, sword, wild beasts
His curse, which unlike theirs is never causeless
A literal fulfilment: the archers who wounded Saul
A shaft from a greater archer, already on the string while they bent their bows

debates.q: What does the last verse say the upright will do?

sides.view: Glory in God, for the honour of his justice rather than the ruin of the wicked
Perhaps rather shine forth clear — have their cause acknowledged just, as the Greek and Latin took it
See that God does not abandon his followers to the malice of bad men

outliers.view: Explains the flight of onlookers as courtiers abandoning a fallen persecutor, asking who would go near Herod when the worms are eating him
